Soil Machine Dynamics Laboratory

Testing methods and physics-based models of soil-to-machine interaction for tires, tracks and tools.

Visit the lab website Email the lab

Overview

The lab develops testing methodology and physics-based modeling of soil-to-machine interaction for agriculture, construction, transportation, infrastructure, and mobility systems, including tires, tracks, and tractive devices.

Facilities and equipment

Three soil testing systems have been developed at the Soil Machine Dynamics Laboratory, located at Iowa State University in Boone, Iowa.

1. Single-tire tester for mobility studies

A mobility soil bin (27 m long, 1.4 m wide and 0.5 m deep), currently filled with cohesive-frictional soils created by mixing sand, clay and oil. The bin's mechanical, electrical, control and measurement systems prepare the soil and run tire and track tests for tractive technology development, mobility, and soil-tire performance studies.

  • Soil is prepared with a rotary tiller, a bucket-blade leveler and a load-driven roller to create uniform or stratified soil layers.
  • Initial soil bulk density can be set from 1.2 Mg/m³ to 1.7 Mg/m³.
  • A PLC (mainly in manual mode) sets operating speed, depth and roller loads.
  • Free-towing and powered tire or track tests with slip control are possible.

2. Blade bin testing

A soil bin 15 m long, 1.5 m wide and 0.25 m deep for testing scaled blades and other soil-cutting tools. Tool motion for scaled bulldozer blades, wheel-loader buckets, ripper teeth and grader blades can be controlled at a similar scale to full machine operating parameters in three axes, with rotational motion also possible. Soil reaction forces, moments and soil rupture are measured with an instrumented data acquisition system calibrated to field soil and gravel conditions.

3. Circular soil bin for ground-engaging tool wear studies

A 4.8 m outer-diameter, 0.4 m deep drum filled with an abrasive medium. Four testing arms (two for tillage tools, two for reconditioning blades) are driven by a 37 kW electric motor with gear-ratio selection, giving arm speeds from 0 to 5.4 m/s. It is used for tool performance and wear modeling, for example tungsten-carbide hardening of cultivator sweeps and seed-opening tools.

Data and soil characterization

Besides technology and tire-performance tests, the data can be used to validate physical system models and algorithms, such as tractive-efficiency optimization for different tire and soil parameters. Soil can be characterized in the laboratory with standard procedures (triaxial, direct shear, Proctor and similar tests) and simple tests (shear vane, cone penetrometer, bevameter).

Soils and test materials

Artificial soil, Clarion series loam soil, sandy soil, clay soil (60% clay fraction), pea gravel, and limestone gravel.

Other options: able to create simulants · bring your own.
